caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

contextLabel.description: Short header tying the suggestion to the user request.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

keywords.description: Topic keywords from the user's request.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__batch
tools.description: Create a doc, or apply several operations to one doc atomically.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__guide
tools.description: Docs guides: topic.instructions repeats the server instructions. Read it only if your client dropped them. Also topic.<name>, refusal.<code>. After a doc's birth → ["topic.index"].

items.description: topic.<name> (instructions, index, editing, tabs, comments, charts, chart-definition, diagram, uploads, sharing, skill) or refusal.<code>; several per call is fine.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__update
tools.description: Edit a tab's contents, rename a doc or tab, or change a stored value.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

task_id.description: The task_id the start_session proposal returned.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task being moved.

remaining_plan.description: What is left to do: steps, files, what done looks like.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context
tools.description: Read context from an embedded interactive widget. Widgets are rendered alongside chat from prior tool calls and can be interacted with by the user. Call this when you need to know the current state of a widget.

tool_name.description: The name of the widget tool to get context for

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list

/reportsounrelatedendpointsremainavailable,andstatewhat/reportshouldreturnwhen

# ARCHITECTURE — Certificate Admin Console

Single source of truth for the Ocean AI Labs take-home (1-hour sitting).
Classification: **(A) standard web application** — no LLM/agent decomposition. Plain layered architecture.

## 0. Hard constraints pulled from the brief

| Constraint | Decision |
|---|---|
| Backend Go/Python/Node + SQLite/MySQL/Postgres | **FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`, WAL mode)** — already scaffolded |
| Frontend Vue 3 / React | **Next.js 15 App Router (React, TS, Tailwind)** — already scaffolded |
| One startup command | `docker compose up --build` (installs deps, seeds demo data, starts both). Fallback: `make dev` (local venv + npm) |
| Actor identification, no login | Header `X-Actor: alice@east.test` → admin → tenant. Unknown → 401 |
| No prod auth / cloud / notifications | Out of scope. No extra features |
| Section 6 `written-answers.md` | **Candidate-only. AI never reads, drafts, edits, or polishes it.** Recorded in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` |
| AI evidence | `ai/sessions/` (Claude Code JSONL from `~/.claude/projects/`), `ai/session-index.csv`, `ai/decision-log.md`, completeness declaration in README |

Note: Section 7 of the brief sums to 180 min; you said 1 hour — the budget below assumes **60 min of build time**.

## 1. Data model (SQLite, `backend/schema.sql`)

```
tenants          id, code (EAST|WEST), name, timezone (Australia/Sydney | Australia/Perth)
admins           id, tenant_id, email UNIQUE
learners         id, tenant_id, name
courses          id, tenant_id, title
enrollments      id, tenant_id, learner_id, course_id, completed_at_utc NULL
                 UNIQUE(learner_id, course_id)
certificates     id, tenant_id, enrollment_id UNIQUE, learner_id, course_id,
                 learner_name, course_title            -- snapshot at issuance (no joins for list/sort/export)
                 serial UNIQUE, status ('active'|'revoked'),
                 issued_at_utc, issued_local_date (YYYY-MM-DD, tenant tz, computed at write),
                 revoked_at_utc NULL
                 INDEX (tenant_id, issued_local_date, id), (tenant_id, learner_name, id), (tenant_id, serial)
audit_events     id, tenant_id, actor_id, action ('certificate.issued'|'certificate.revoked'),
                 certificate_id, operation_id NULL, created_at_utc
                 INDEX (certificate_id)
idempotency_keys tenant_id, key, request_hash, status ('in_progress'|'done'),
                 response_json NULL, created_at_utc
                 PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, key)
```

Invariants enforced by the DB, not just code:
- `certificates.enrollment_id UNIQUE` → at most one certificate per enrollment (A2/A4 safety net).
- `idempotency_keys PK (tenant_id, key)` → one logical operation per key per tenant (A2/A3).
- All tables carry `tenant_id`; every query is `WHERE tenant_id = :actor_tenant` (A1).

## 2. Data flow

```
 Browser (Next.js)                               FastAPI                              SQLite (WAL)
 ───────────────                                 ───────                              ────────────
 actor selector ──X-Actor header──▶ deps.get_actor() ──▶ admins ⨝ tenants ──▶ Actor{tenant_id, tz}
                                         │
 list page  ──GET /api/certificates──▶ routers.certificates ─▶ services.certificates.query()
   q,sort,dir,page                       │                      whitelist sort col + ", id ASC"
                                         │                      LIKE on learner_name/serial ──▶ SELECT … LIMIT/OFFSET
                                         ◀── {items,total,page,page_size}  (issued_at_local formatted via zoneinfo)
 export btn ──GET …/export.csv──▶ StreamingResponse(csv_rows())  opens its OWN connection
   same q,sort,dir                       │   inside the generator thread, fetchmany(2000) ──▶ SELECT … ORDER BY sort,id
                                         │                                                   (no OFFSET; single cursor)
 bulk issue ──POST /bulk-issue──▶ services.issuance.bulk_issue()
   {course_id} + Idempotency-Key         │   BEGIN IMMEDIATE  (serialises writers; busy_timeout 30s)
                                         │   INSERT idempotency_keys  ─ conflict? ─▶ hash≠ → 409 | done → replay response
                                         │   course ∈ tenant? else 404 (nothing written)
                                         │   for each enrollment in course: completed? certified? → issued/skipped
                                         │   INSERT certificate + INSERT audit(issued) per issuance
                                         │   UPDATE idempotency_keys SET done, response_json
                                         │   COMMIT
 detail page ──GET /api/certificates/{id}──▶ cert WHERE id AND tenant_id → 404 if other tenant
 revoke   ──POST …/{id}/revoke──▶ BEGIN IMMEDIATE; UPDATE … SET revoked WHERE id AND tenant_id AND status='active'
                                         │   rowcount==1 → INSERT audit(revoked); rowcount==0 → no audit (A7 repeat)
                                         │   COMMIT → return detail
```

## 3. Component breakdown (separation of concerns)

### Backend `backend/` (flat package, run from `backend/`)
| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `main.py` | FastAPI app, CORS (`http://localhost:3000`), router mounting, `/health`, startup: ensure schema + seed if empty |
| `config.py` | `DB_PATH`, CORS origins (pydantic-settings) |
| `db.py` | `connect()` per request: WAL, `busy_timeout=30000`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `row_factory=Row`, `isolation_level=None`; `write_txn()` ctx-manager issuing `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` |
| `schema.sql` | DDL above |
| `seed.py` | `python seed.py` quick-start dataset (idempotent); `python seed.py --big EAST --rows 100000` generator (batched executemany, deliberately repeated names/dates for equal sort keys). Big mode never touches quick-start rows |
| `deps.py` | `get_actor(X-Actor)` → `Actor(id, email, tenant_id, tenant_code, tz)`; 401 on unknown |
| `tz.py` | `utc_to_local(iso, tz) -> (local_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM')` via `zoneinfo` |
| `schemas.py` | Pydantic response/request models, error shape `{detail:{code,message}}` |
| `routers/actors.py` | `GET /api/actors` (seeded admins for selector), `GET /api/me` |
| `routers/courses.py` | `GET /api/courses` (tenant-scoped) |
| `routers/certificates.py` | list / export.csv / detail / revoke / bulk-issue — HTTP only, delegates |
| `services/certificates.py` | query builder (search, whitelisted sort + id tiebreak, pagination), detail+audit, revoke, CSV row iterator |
| `services/issuance.py` | bulk issue with idempotency + per-learner outcomes |
| `tests/test_acceptance.py` | A1–A7 via `TestClient` on a temp DB; A2 concurrency with `ThreadPoolExecutor`; A6 marked `big` |
| `Dockerfile` | python:3.12-slim, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, CMD `python seed.py && uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0` |

### API surface
```
GET  /health
GET  /api/actors                         -> [{email, tenant_code}]
GET  /api/me                             -> {email, tenant:{code,name,timezone}}
GET  /api/courses                        -> [{id,title}]
GET  /api/certificates?q&sort&dir&page&page_size
     sort ∈ issued_local_date(default desc)|learner_name|serial|course_title|status ; always + ", id ASC"
     -> {items:[{id,serial,learner_name,course_title,status,issued_at_utc,issued_at_local,issued_local_date}], total, page, page_size}
GET  /api/certificates/export.csv?q&sort&dir   -> text/csv stream: learner_name,course_title,serial,issued_local_date
GET  /api/certificates/{id}              -> detail + audit:[{action,actor_email,created_at_utc,operation_id}]
POST /api/certificates/{id}/revoke       -> detail (200 even if already revoked; audit only on transition)
POST /api/certificates/bulk-issue  {course_id}  header Idempotency-Key (required, 400 if missing)
     -> {operation_id, replayed:bool, summary:{issued,skipped,failed},
         results:[{learner_id,learner_name,outcome:'issued'|'skipped'|'failed',reason,serial}]}
     409 on same key + different payload
```

### Frontend `frontend/src/`
| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `lib/api.ts` | `fetch` wrapper: base URL from `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, attaches `X-Actor` from localStorage, normalises errors |
| `lib/actor.tsx` | `ActorProvider` + selector (persists choice; reloads data on change) |
| `app/page.tsx` | Certificate list: search input, sortable headers, pagination, **loading / empty / error** states, Export CSV (fetch→blob→download with same q/sort/dir), Bulk-issue panel |
| `components/BulkIssuePanel.tsx` | course select; idempotency key generated once per attempt and reused on retry; button disabled while pending; status + per-learner outcome table |
| `app/certificates/[id]/page.tsx` | detail fields (serial, course, learner, tenant-local issue date, status), Revoke with `confirm()`, audit list |

No extra client libs. Tailwind only for layout.

### Root
```
fastapi-app/                 (rename to cert-admin-console at git init — optional)
├── ARCHITECTURE.md  CLAUDE.md  AGENTS.md  README.md
├── docker-compose.yml   Makefile (dev / verify / verify-big / big-data)
├── backend/   frontend/
├── ai/sessions/  ai/session-index.csv  ai/decision-log.md
└── written-answers.md       ← candidate-only, AI-excluded
```

## 4. Acceptance scenario → mechanism

| ID | Mechanism | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| A1 Tenant isolation | `tenant_id` from actor on every query; detail/course lookup scoped → 404; bulk-issue course check happens inside txn **before** any insert, so rejection writes nothing | test: bob hits East cert id → 404; bob bulk-issues East course → 404, cert/audit counts unchanged |
| A2 Retry safety | `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + PK on `(tenant_id,key)`: concurrent duplicates block on the write lock, then replay stored `response_json`; `enrollment_id UNIQUE` as backstop | test: 5 threads same key → identical bodies, certs = eligible count, audit = certs |
| A3 Key misuse | `request_hash = sha256(canonical json)` compared on key hit → 409, first result untouched | test |
| A4 Outcomes | eligibility = `completed_at_utc IS NOT NULL AND no certificate for enrollment`; skip reasons `not_completed` / `already_certified`; per-row try/except → `failed` | test on seeded Safety 101 |
| A5 DST / local date | `issued_local_date` computed with `zoneinfo` at write; display string computed at read; sort/CSV use `issued_local_date` | seed both tenants with `2026-01-10T13:30:00Z`; assert `2026-01-11 00:30` (East) / `2026-01-10 21:30` (West) |
| A6 Export growth | streaming CSV, own connection per generator, `fetchmany`, index on `(tenant_id, issued_local_date, id)`, deterministic `ORDER BY sort, id`; WAL lets list reads proceed during export | `make verify-big`: generate 100k, export twice with q+sort, diff identical, each < 60 s, list call succeeds mid-export |
| A7 Revocation audit | conditional `UPDATE … AND status='active'`; audit only when `rowcount == 1` | test: revoke twice → 1 audit row |

## 5. Time budget (60 min build)

| Min | Work | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 | `git init`, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (incl. Section-6 exclusion), `schema.sql`, `db.py`, `seed.py` quick-start | `chore: scaffold + schema + seed` |
| 5–22 | backend: deps, tz, services, routers, bulk-issue idempotency, streaming export | `feat: certificate API A1–A7` |
| 22–35 | frontend: actor selector, list (states/sort/search/paging/export), bulk panel, detail+revoke | `feat: admin console UI` |
| 35–45 | `tests/test_acceptance.py` A1–A5, A7 + `--big` generator + A6 script; fix defects | `test: acceptance A1–A7` |
| 45–53 | Dockerfiles, compose, Makefile, README (startup, headers, repro steps, 100k, known defects) | `docs: README + startup` |
| 53–60 | copy Claude Code JSONL → `ai/sessions/`, `session-index.csv`, `decision-log.md`, completeness declaration, final commit | `docs: AI evidence` |
| after | **You alone**: `written-answers.md` | your commit |

Cut order if over time: (1) Docker → `make dev` only, (2) sort on status/course_title, (3) audit list in UI (keep in API).

## 6. Open decisions for you
1. Startup command: `docker compose up --build` (your Docker-first preference) with `make dev` fallback — **default**, or local-only to save ~5 min?
2. Repo folder name stays `fastapi-app` or rename to `cert-admin-console`?

                                         ◀── {items,total,page,page_size}  (issued_at_local formatted via zoneinfo)
 export btn ──GET …/export.csv──▶ StreamingResponse(csv_rows())  opens its OWN connection
   same q,sort,dir                       │   inside the generator thread, fetchmany(2000) ──▶ SELECT … ORDER BY sort,id
                                         │                                                   (no OFFSET; single cursor)
 bulk issue ──POST /bulk-issue──▶ services.issuance.bulk_issue()
   {course_id} + Idempotency-Key         │   BEGIN IMMEDIATE  (serialises writers; busy_timeout 30s)
                                         │   INSERT idempotency_keys  ─ conflict? ─▶ hash≠ → 409 | done → replay response
                                         │   course ∈ tenant? else 404 (nothing written)
                                         │   for each enrollment in course: completed? certified? → issued/skipped
                                         │   INSERT certificate + INSERT audit(issued) per issuance
                                         │   UPDATE idempotency_keys SET done, response_json
                                         │   COMMIT
 detail page ──GET /api/certificates/{id}──▶ cert WHERE id AND tenant_id → 404 if other tenant
 revoke   ──POST …/{id}/revoke──▶ BEGIN IMMEDIATE; UPDATE … SET revoked WHERE id AND tenant_id AND status='active'
                                         │   rowcount==1 → INSERT audit(revoked); rowcount==0 → no audit (A7 repeat)
                                         │   COMMIT → return detail
```

## 3. Component breakdown (separation of concerns)

### Backend `backend/` (flat package, run from `backend/`)
| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `main.py` | FastAPI app, CORS (`http://localhost:3000`), router mounting, `/health`, startup: ensure schema + seed if empty |
| `config.py` | `DB_PATH`, CORS origins (pydantic-settings) |
| `db.py` | `connect()` per request: WAL, `busy_timeout=30000`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `row_factory=Row`, `isolation_level=None`; `write_txn()` ctx-manager issuing `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` |
| `schema.sql` | DDL above |
| `seed.py` | `python seed.py` quick-start dataset (idempotent); `python seed.py --big EAST --rows 100000` generator (batched executemany, deliberately repeated names/dates for equal sort keys). Big mode never touches quick-start rows |
| `deps.py` | `get_actor(X-Actor)` → `Actor(id, email, tenant_id, tenant_code, tz)`; 401 on unknown |
| `tz.py` | `utc_to_local(iso, tz) -> (local_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM')` via `zoneinfo` |
| `schemas.py` | Pydantic response/request models, error shape `{detail:{code,message}}` |
| `routers/actors.py` | `GET /api/actors` (seeded admins for selector), `GET /api/me` |
| `routers/courses.py` | `GET /api/courses` (tenant-scoped) |
| `routers/certificates.py` | list / export.csv / detail / revoke / bulk-issue — HTTP only, delegates |
| `services/certificates.py` | query builder (search, whitelisted sort + id tiebreak, pagination), detail+audit, revoke, CSV row iterator |
| `services/issuance.py` | bulk issue with idempotency + per-learner outcomes |
| `tests/test_acceptance.py` | A1–A7 via `TestClient` on a temp DB; A2 concurrency with `ThreadPoolExecutor`; A6 marked `big` |
| `Dockerfile` | python:3.12-slim, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, CMD `python seed.py && uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0` |

### API surface
```
GET  /health
GET  /api/actors                         -> [{email, tenant_code}]
GET  /api/me                             -> {email, tenant:{code,name,timezone}}
GET  /api/courses                        -> [{id,title}]
GET  /api/certificates?q&sort&dir&page&page_size
     sort ∈ issued_local_date(default desc)|learner_name|serial|course_title|status ; always + ", id ASC"
     -> {items:[{id,serial,learner_name,course_title,status,issued_at_utc,issued_at_local,issued_local_date}], total, page, page_size}
GET  /api/certificates/export.csv?q&sort&dir   -> text/csv stream: learner_name,course_title,serial,issued_local_date
GET  /api/certificates/{id}              -> detail + audit:[{action,actor_email,created_at_utc,operation_id}]
POST /api/certificates/{id}/revoke       -> detail (200 even if already revoked; audit only on transition)
POST /api/certificates/bulk-issue  {course_id}  header Idempotency-Key (required, 400 if missing)
     -> {operation_id, replayed:bool, summary:{issued,skipped,failed},
         results:[{learner_id,learner_name,outcome:'issued'|'skipped'|'failed',reason,serial}]}
     409 on same key + different payload
```

### Frontend `frontend/src/`
| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `lib/api.ts` | `fetch` wrapper: base URL from `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, attaches `X-Actor` from localStorage, normalises errors |
| `lib/actor.tsx` | `ActorProvider` + selector (persists choice; reloads data on change) |
| `app/page.tsx` | Certificate list: search input, sortable headers, pagination, **loading / empty / error** states, Export CSV (fetch→blob→download with same q/sort/dir), Bulk-issue panel |
| `components/BulkIssuePanel.tsx` | course select; idempotency key generated once per attempt and reused on retry; button disabled while pending; status + per-learner outcome table |
| `app/certificates/[id]/page.tsx` | detail fields (serial, course, learner, tenant-local issue date, status), Revoke with `confirm()`, audit list |

No extra client libs. Tailwind only for layout.

```
fastapi-app/                 (rename to cert-admin-console at git init — optional)
├── ARCHITECTURE.md  CLAUDE.md  AGENTS.md  README.md
├── docker-compose.yml   Makefile (dev / verify / verify-big / big-data)
├── backend/   frontend/
├── ai/sessions/  ai/session-index.csv  ai/decision-log.md

import contextlib
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from config import settings

SCHEMA_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("schema.sql")


def connect(db_path: str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """One connection per request/thread. Autocommit mode; writes go through write_txn()."""
    path = Path(db_path or settings.db_path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
    return conn


def init_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text())


@contextlib.contextmanager
def write_txn(conn: sqlite3.Connection):
    """BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock up front, so concurrent writers queue
    (up to busy_timeout) instead of racing. Everything inside is one atomic unit."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        yield conn
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    else:
        conn.execute("COMMIT")


def get_db():
    conn = connect()
    try:
        yield conn
    finally:
        conn.close()

import contextlib
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from config import settings

SCHEMA_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("schema.sql")


def connect(db_path: str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """One connection per request/thread. Autocommit mode; writes go through write_txn()."""
    path = Path(db_path or settings.db_path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
    return conn


def init_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text())


@contextlib.contextmanager
def write_txn(conn: sqlite3.Connection):
    """BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock up front, so concurrent writers queue
    (up to busy_timeout) instead of racing. Everything inside is one atomic unit."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        yield conn
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    else:
        conn.execute("COMMIT")


def get_db():
    conn = connect()
    try:
        yield conn
    finally:
        conn.close()

    t = conn.execute("SELECT id, timezone FROM tenants WHERE code=?", (tenant_code,)).fetchone()
    if not t:
        sys.exit(f"unknown tenant {tenant_code}")
    tid, tz_name = t["id"], t["timezone"]
    aid = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM admins WHERE tenant_id=?", (tid,)).fetchone()["id"]
    if conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM courses WHERE tenant_id=? AND title LIKE 'Bulk Course %'", (tid,)).fetchone():
        sys.exit(f"{tenant_code} already has generated data; delete the DB to regenerate")

    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    n_courses = 20
    n_learners = -(-rows // n_courses)  # ceil
    names = [f"{f} {l}" for f in FIRST for l in LAST]  # 120 names -> heavy key repetition
    base = parse_utc("2025-06-01T00:00:00Z")

    def next_id(table):
        return (conn.execute(f"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id),0) FROM {table}").fetchone()[0]) + 1

    with write_txn(conn):
        course_ids = [
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO courses(tenant_id,title) VALUES (?,?)", (tid, f"Bulk Course {i:02d}")).lastrowid
            for i in range(1, n_courses + 1)
        ]
        l0 = next_id("learners")
        learner_rows = [(l0 + i, tid, names[i % len(names)]) for i in range(n_learners)]
        conn.executemany("INSERT INTO learners(id,tenant_id,name) VALUES (?,?,?)", learner_rows)

        e0, c0, a0 = next_id("enrollments"), next_id("certificates"), next_id("audit_events")
        enrolls, certs, audits = [], [], []
        for i in range(rows):
            li, ci = i % n_learners, i // n_learners
            learner_id, learner_name = learner_rows[li][0], learner_rows[li][2]
            course_id = course_ids[ci]
            issued_dt = base + timedelta(seconds=rnd.randrange(0, 200 * 86400))
            issued_utc = issued_dt.strftime(UTC_FMT)
            local_date, _ = to_local(issued_utc, tz_name)
            status = "revoked" if i % 50 == 0 else "active"
            enrolls.append((e0 + i, tid, learner_id, course_id, issued_utc))
            certs.append((c0 + i, tid, e0 + i, learner_id, course_id, learner_name, f"Bulk Course {ci + 1:02d}",
                          f"{tenant_code}-G{i + 1:07d}", status, issued_utc, local_date,
                          issued_utc if status == "revoked" else None))
            audits.append((a0 + i, tid, aid, "certificate.issued", c0 + i, "generator", issued_utc))
        conn.executemany("INSERT INTO enrollments(id,tenant_id,learner_id,course_id,completed_at_utc) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)", enrolls)

            """INSERT INTO certificates(id,tenant_id,enrollment_id,learner_id,course_id,learner_name,course_title,
               serial,status,issued_at_utc,issued_local_date,revoked_at_utc) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""", certs)
        conn.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO audit_events(id,tenant_id,actor_id,action,certificate_id,operation_id,created_at_utc) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            audits)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--big", metavar="TENANT_CODE", help="append generated certificates to this tenant")
    ap.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=100_000)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    conn = connect()
    init_schema(conn)
    created = seed_quick(conn)
    print("quick-start data:", "created" if created else "already present")
    if args.big:
        seed_big(conn, args.big.upper(), args.rows)
        print(f"generated {args.rows} certificates for {args.big.upper()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import uuid

from db import write_txn
from deps import Actor, err
from tz import now_utc_iso, to_local


def new_serial(tenant_code: str) -> str:
    return f"{tenant_code}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10].upper()}"


def issue_certificate(conn, actor: Actor, enrollment_id: int, learner_id: int, course_id: int,
                      learner_name: str, course_title: str, issued_at_utc: str, operation_id: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """One certificate + exactly one 'issued' audit event, inside the caller's transaction."""
    serial = new_serial(actor.tenant_code)
    local_date, _ = to_local(issued_at_utc, actor.tz)
    cert_id = conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO certificates(tenant_id, enrollment_id, learner_id, course_id, learner_name,
               course_title, serial, status, issued_at_utc, issued_local_date)
           VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,'active',?,?)""",
        (actor.tenant_id, enrollment_id, learner_id, course_id, learner_name, course_title,
         serial, issued_at_utc, local_date),
    ).lastrowid
    conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO audit_events(tenant_id, actor_id, action, certificate_id, operation_id, created_at_utc)
           VALUES (?,?,'certificate.issued',?,?,?)""",
        (actor.tenant_id, actor.id, cert_id, operation_id, issued_at_utc),
    )
    return cert_id, serial


def bulk_issue(conn, actor: Actor, course_id: int, idempotency_key: str) -> dict:
    """Whole operation is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction keyed by (tenant, idempotency key).

    Concurrent duplicates queue on the write lock; when they get it the key row already exists
    and they replay the stored response (A2). Same key + different payload -> 409 (A3).
    A cross-tenant course -> 404 and the transaction rolls back, so nothing persists (A1).
    """
    request_hash = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({"course_id": course_id}, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    operation_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    now = now_utc_iso()

    with write_txn(conn):
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO idempotency_keys(tenant_id, key, request_hash, status, response_json, created_at_utc) "
                "VALUES (?,?,?,'in_progress',NULL,?)",
                (actor.tenant_id, idempotency_key, request_hash, now),
            )
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_hash, status, response_json FROM idempotency_keys WHERE tenant_id = ? AND key = ?",
                (actor.tenant_id, idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            if row["request_hash"] != request_hash:
                raise err(409, "idempotency_key_reused",
                          "Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request payload")
            if row["status"] == "done":
                return {**json.loads(row["response_json"]), "replayed": True}
            raise err(409, "operation_in_progress", "the same operation is still in progress")

        course = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, title FROM courses WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?", (course_id, actor.tenant_id)
        ).fetchone()
        if not course:
            raise err(404, "course_not_found", f"course {course_id} not found")

        rows = conn.execute(
            """SELECT e.id AS enrollment_id, e.learner_id, l.name AS learner_name, e.completed_at_utc,
                      c.id AS cert_id, c.serial
               FROM enrollments e
               JOIN learners l ON l.id = e.learner_id
               LEFT JOIN certificates c ON c.enrollment_id = e.id
               WHERE e.course_id = ? AND e.tenant_id = ?
               ORDER BY l.name, e.id""",
            (course_id, actor.tenant_id),
        ).fetchall()

        summary = {"issued": 0, "skipped": 0, "failed": 0}
        results = []
        for r in rows:
            serial = None
            if r["cert_id"]:
                outcome, reason, serial = "skipped", "already_certified", r["serial"]
            elif not r["completed_at_utc"]:
                outcome, reason = "skipped", "not_completed"
            else:
                try:
                    _, serial = issue_certificate(conn, actor, r["enrollment_id"], r["learner_id"], course["id"],
                                                  r["learner_name"], course["title"], now, operation_id)
                    outcome, reason = "issued", None
                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                    outcome, reason = "failed", f"constraint violation: {exc}"
            summary[outcome] += 1
            results.append({"learner_id": r["learner_id"], "learner_name": r["learner_name"],
                            "outcome": outcome, "reason": reason, "serial": serial})

        response = {
            "operation_id": operation_id,
            "course_id": course["id"],
            "course_title": course["title"],
            "summary": summary,
            "results": results,
            "replayed": False,
        }
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE idempotency_keys SET status = 'done', response_json = ? WHERE tenant_id = ? AND key = ?",
            (json.dumps(response), actor.tenant_id, idempotency_key),
        )
    return response

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

from config import settings
from db import connect, init_schema
from routers import actors, certificates
from seed import seed_quick


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI):
    conn = connect()
    try:
        init_schema(conn)
        seed_quick(conn)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    yield


app = FastAPI(title=settings.app_name, lifespan=lifespan)

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
    expose_headers=["Content-Disposition"],

import json
import sqlite3
import uuid

from db import write_txn
from deps import Actor, err
from tz import now_utc_iso, to_local


def new_serial(tenant_code: str) -> str:
    return f"{tenant_code}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10].upper()}"


def issue_certificate(conn, actor: Actor, enrollment_id: int, learner_id: int, course_id: int,
                      learner_name: str, course_title: str, issued_at_utc: str, operation_id: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """One certificate + exactly one 'issued' audit event, inside the caller's transaction."""
    serial = new_serial(actor.tenant_code)
    local_date, _ = to_local(issued_at_utc, actor.tz)
    cert_id = conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO certificates(tenant_id, enrollment_id, learner_id, course_id, learner_name,
               course_title, serial, status, issued_at_utc, issued_local_date)
           VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,'active',?,?)""",
        (actor.tenant_id, enrollment_id, learner_id, course_id, learner_name, course_title,
         serial, issued_at_utc, local_date),
    ).lastrowid
    conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO audit_events(tenant_id, actor_id, action, certificate_id, operation_id, created_at_utc)
           VALUES (?,?,'certificate.issued',?,?,?)""",
        (actor.tenant_id, actor.id, cert_id, operation_id, issued_at_utc),
    )
    return cert_id, serial

    """Whole operation is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction keyed by (tenant, idempotency key).

    Concurrent duplicates queue on the write lock; when they get it the key row already exists
    and they replay the stored response (A2). Same key + different payload -> 409 (A3).
    A cross-tenant course -> 404 and the transaction rolls back, so nothing persists (A1).
    """
    request_hash = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({"course_id": course_id}, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    operation_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    now = now_utc_iso()

    with write_txn(conn):
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO idempotency_keys(tenant_id, key, request_hash, status, response_json, created_at_utc) "
                "VALUES (?,?,?,'in_progress',NULL,?)",
                (actor.tenant_id, idempotency_key, request_hash, now),
            )
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_hash, status, response_json FROM idempotency_keys WHERE tenant_id = ? AND key = ?",
                (actor.tenant_id, idempotency_key),
            ).fetchone()
            if row["request_hash"] != request_hash:
                raise err(409, "idempotency_key_reused",
                          "Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request payload")
            if row["status"] == "done":
                return {**json.loads(row["response_json"]), "replayed": True}
            raise err(409, "operation_in_progress", "the same operation is still in progress")

        course = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, title FROM courses WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?", (course_id, actor.tenant_id)
        ).fetchone()
        if not course:
            raise err(404, "course_not_found", f"course {course_id} not found")

        rows = conn.execute(
            """SELECT e.id AS enrollment_id, e.learner_id, l.name AS learner_name, e.completed_at_utc,
                      c.id AS cert_id, c.serial
               FROM enrollments e
               JOIN learners l ON l.id = e.learner_id
               LEFT JOIN certificates c ON c.enrollment_id = e.id
               WHERE e.course_id = ? AND e.tenant_id = ?
               ORDER BY l.name, e.id""",
            (course_id, actor.tenant_id),
        ).fetchall()

        summary = {"issued": 0, "skipped": 0, "failed": 0}
        results = []
        for r in rows:
            serial = None
            if r["cert_id"]:
                outcome, reason, serial = "skipped", "already_certified", r["serial"]
            elif not r["completed_at_utc"]:
                outcome, reason = "skipped", "not_completed"
            else:

                                                  r["learner_name"], course["title"], now, operation_id)
                    outcome, reason = "issued", None
                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                    outcome, reason = "failed", f"constraint violation: {exc}"
            summary[outcome] += 1
            results.append({"learner_id": r["learner_id"], "learner_name": r["learner_name"],
                            "outcome": outcome, "reason": reason, "serial": serial})

        response = {
            "operation_id": operation_id,
            "course_id": course["id"],
            "course_title": course["title"],
            "summary": summary,
            "results": results,
            "replayed": False,
        }
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE idempotency_keys SET status = 'done', response_json = ? WHERE tenant_id = ? AND key = ?",
            (json.dumps(response), actor.tenant_id, idempotency_key),
        )
    return response

"""A1-A7 from the brief. Tests share one seeded temp DB and run in file order."""
import threading
import time
import uuid
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from db import connect
from main import app

ALICE = {"X-Actor": "alice@east.test"}
BOB = {"X-Actor": "bob@west.test"}
CERTS = "/api/certificates"
EXPORT = "/api/certificates/export.csv"


def list_certs(client, headers, **params):
    r = client.get(CERTS, headers=headers, params={"page_size": 100, **params})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


def find(client, headers, serial):
    items = list_certs(client, headers, q=serial)["items"]
    assert len(items) == 1
    return items[0]


def course_id(client, headers, title):
    return next(c["id"] for c in client.get("/api/courses", headers=headers).json() if c["title"] == title)


def db_count(sql, *params):
    conn = connect()
    try:
        return conn.execute(sql, params).fetchone()[0]
    finally:
        conn.close()


def strip_replayed(body):
    return {k: v for k, v in body.items() if k != "replayed"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A5
def test_a5_dst_and_tenant_local_date(client):
    east = find(client, ALICE, "EAST-SEED-0001")
    west = find(client, BOB, "WEST-SEED-0001")
    assert east["issued_at_utc"] == west["issued_at_utc"] == "2026-01-10T13:30:00Z"
    assert (east["issued_at_local"], east["issued_local_date"]) == ("2026-01-11 00:30", "2026-01-11")
    assert (west["issued_at_local"], west["issued_local_date"]) == ("2026-01-10 21:30", "2026-01-10")
    csv_east = client.get(EXPORT, headers=ALICE, params={"q": "EAST-SEED-0001"}).text
    assert "Jordan Kim,Safety 101,EAST-SEED-0001,2026-01-11" in csv_east
    csv_west = client.get(EXPORT, headers=BOB, params={"q": "WEST-SEED-0001"}).text
    assert "Jordan Kim,Safety 101,WEST-SEED-0001,2026-01-10" in csv_west
    # list sorts by the tenant-local calendar date, ascending => Maria (2026-01-01 Sydney) before Jordan
    items = list_certs(client, ALICE, sort="issued_local_date", dir="asc")["items"]
    dates = [i["issued_local_date"] for i in items]
    assert dates == sorted(dates)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A1
def test_a1_tenant_isolation(client):
    west_items = list_certs(client, BOB)["items"]
    assert west_items and all(i["serial"].startswith("WEST-") for i in west_items)
    csv_text = client.get(EXPORT, headers=BOB).text
    assert "WEST-" in csv_text and "EAST-" not in csv_text

    east_cert = find(client, ALICE, "EAST-SEED-0001")
    assert client.get(f"{CERTS}/{east_cert['id']}", headers=BOB).status_code == 404
    assert client.post(f"{CERTS}/{east_cert['id']}/revoke", headers=BOB).status_code == 404
    assert find(client, ALICE, "EAST-SEED-0001")["status"] == "active"

    east_safety = course_id(client, ALICE, "Safety 101")
    certs_before, audit_before = db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM certificates"), db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_events")
    r = client.post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers={**BOB, "Idempotency-Key": "bob-cross-tenant"},
                    json={"course_id": east_safety})
    assert r.status_code == 404
    assert db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM certificates") == certs_before
    assert db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_events") == audit_before
    assert db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM idempotency_keys WHERE key='bob-cross-tenant'") == 0

    assert client.get(CERTS).status_code == 401
    assert client.get(CERTS, headers={"X-Actor": "mallory@nowhere.test"}).status_code == 401


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A2 + A4
KEY = "alice-safety-" + uuid.uuid4().hex
FIRST_RESPONSE = {}


def test_a2_a4_bulk_issue_outcomes_and_retry_safety(client):
    cid = course_id(client, ALICE, "Safety 101")
    headers = {**ALICE, "Idempotency-Key": KEY}

    r1 = client.post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers=headers, json={"course_id": cid})
    assert r1.status_code == 200, r1.text
    body = r1.json()
    FIRST_RESPONSE.update(body)
    assert body["replayed"] is False
    assert body["summary"] == {"issued": 2, "skipped": 3, "failed": 0}
    outcomes = {x["learner_name"]: (x["outcome"], x["reason"]) for x in body["results"]}
    assert outcomes == {
        "Alex Lee": ("issued", None),
        "Priya Nair": ("issued", None),
        "Sam Chen": ("skipped", "not_completed"),
        "Jordan Kim": ("skipped", "already_certified"),
        "Maria Garcia": ("skipped", "already_certified"),
    }

    # sequential retry
    r2 = client.post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers=headers, json={"course_id": cid})
    assert r2.status_code == 200 and r2.json()["replayed"] is True
    assert strip_replayed(r2.json()) == strip_replayed(body)

    # concurrent retries: each thread gets its own client (own connection)
    def call(_):
        return TestClient(app).post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers=headers, json={"course_id": cid})

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as ex:
        responses = list(ex.map(call, range(8)))
    assert all(r.status_code == 200 for r in responses), [r.text for r in responses]
    assert all(strip_replayed(r.json()) == strip_replayed(body) for r in responses)

    assert db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM certificates WHERE course_id=?", cid) == 4  # 2 seeded + 2 issued
    assert db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit_events WHERE operation_id=?", body["operation_id"]) == 2
    assert db_count(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT certificate_id FROM audit_events WHERE action='certificate.issued' "
        "GROUP BY certificate_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)") == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A3
def test_a3_key_reuse_with_different_payload(client):
    other = course_id(client, ALICE, "Data Privacy Basics")
    before = db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM certificates")
    r = client.post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers={**ALICE, "Idempotency-Key": KEY}, json={"course_id": other})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["detail"]["code"] == "idempotency_key_reused"
    assert db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM certificates") == before
    # first result untouched
    r2 = client.post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers={**ALICE, "Idempotency-Key": KEY},
                     json={"course_id": FIRST_RESPONSE["course_id"]})
    assert strip_replayed(r2.json()) == strip_replayed(FIRST_RESPONSE)
    # missing key
    assert client.post(f"{CERTS}/bulk-issue", headers=ALICE, json={"course_id": other}).status_code == 400


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A7
def test_a7_revocation_audit_once(client):
    serial = next(x["serial"] for x in FIRST_RESPONSE["results"] if x["learner_name"] == "Alex Lee")
    cert = find(client, ALICE, serial)
    r1 = client.post(f"{CERTS}/{cert['id']}/revoke", headers=ALICE)
    assert r1.status_code == 200 and r1.json()["status"] == "revoked"
    r2 = client.post(f"{CERTS}/{cert['id']}/revoke", headers=ALICE)
    assert r2.status_code == 200 and r2.json()["status"] == "revoked"
    revocations = [a for a in r2.json()["audit"] if a["action"] == "certificate.revoked"]
    issuances = [a for a in r2.json()["audit"] if a["action"] == "certificate.issued"]
    assert len(revocations) == 1 and len(issuances) == 1
    assert revocations[0]["actor_email"] == "alice@east.test"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- list UX basics
def test_list_search_sort_paginate(client):
    page1 = list_certs(client, ALICE, page=1, page_size=2, sort="serial", dir="asc")
    page2 = list_certs(client, ALICE, page=2, page_size=2, sort="serial", dir="asc")
    assert page1["total"] >= 4 and len(page1["items"]) == 2 and len(page2["items"]) == 2
    serials = [i["serial"] for i in page1["items"] + page2["items"]]
    assert serials == sorted(serials)
    assert list_certs(client, ALICE, q="Alex")["items"][0]["learner_name"] == "Alex Lee"
    assert list_certs(client, ALICE, q="zzz-nothing")["items"] == []
    assert client.get(CERTS, headers=ALICE, params={"sort": "id; DROP"}).status_code == 422


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A6 (opt-in: pytest -m big)
@pytest.mark.big
def test_a6_export_growth(client):
    from seed import seed_big

    conn = connect()
    try:
        seed_big(conn, "EAST", 100_000)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    params = {"q": "Lee", "sort": "learner_name", "dir": "asc"}
    expected_total = list_certs(client, ALICE, **params)["total"]
    assert expected_total > 1000

    list_ok = {}

    def list_during_export():
        time.sleep(0.2)
        r = TestClient(app).get(CERTS, headers=ALICE, params={**params, "page": 3})
        list_ok["status"] = r.status_code
        list_ok["elapsed"] = time.perf_counter() - t0

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    probe = threading.Thread(target=list_during_export)
    probe.start()
    first = client.get(EXPORT, headers=ALICE, params=params)
    t_first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    probe.join()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    second = client.get(EXPORT, headers=ALICE, params=params)
    t_second = time.perf_counter() - t0

    assert first.status_code == 200 and second.status_code == 200
    assert t_first < 60 and t_second < 60, (t_first, t_second)
    assert list_ok["status"] == 200
    assert first.content == second.content  # equal sort keys keep relative order (id tiebreak)
    lines = first.text.splitlines()
    assert lines[0] == "learner_name,course_title,serial,issued_local_date"
    rows = [ln.split(",") for ln in lines[1:]]
    assert len(rows) == expected_total
    assert all("Lee" in r[0] or "Lee" in r[2] for r in rows)
    assert all(r[2].startswith("EAST-") for r in rows)
    names = [r[0] for r in rows]
    assert names == sorted(names)
    print(f"\nA6: {len(rows)} rows, export #1 {t_first:.2f}s, #2 {t_second:.2f}s, "
          f"list during export -> {list_ok['status']} after {list_ok['elapsed']:.2f}s")
